# React engineering — full guide

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-guide.mjs. Edit SKILL.md and rules/*.md; regenerate. -->

Use these rules for this repository's React/Vite/Tauri frontend, including supported
stack capabilities and intended MVP surfaces that are not implemented yet.
Applicability determines which rules to read; measurement determines whether a
conditional optimization is warranted.

Read [verification policy](../../../docs/agents/verification.md) before applying
this skill. Read [the MVP](../../../docs/MVP.md) for behavior, architecture, or
execution ownership, and the relevant milestone for its acceptance criteria.
Before component work, read [the component guide](../../../src/components/README.md)
and use [shadcn](../shadcn/SKILL.md) for toolkit APIs and conventions. These owners
remain authoritative; rule examples support their implementation.

## How to use

Use the categorized summaries to select each rule whose decision the task touches,
then read that rule's applicability, examples, and caveats. Higher-impact correctness
and ownership concerns take precedence over optional performance recipes. Impact
labels describe consequences here, not measured speedup estimates.

Examples are focused sketches: ordinary imports and surrounding feature code may
be omitted; illustrative adapters/components are identified rather than presented
as existing product APIs. Use current installed-version docs when implementing.
For a complete reference or broad review, [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) expands all rules.
Individual rules are the editable source; the full guide is generated.

## Components, state and identity

### component-responsibilities

Extract components, Hooks, and plain functions for different responsibilities.

Impact: MEDIUM — Keeps dependencies and update boundaries understandable.

Source: [rules/component-responsibilities.md](rules/component-responsibilities.md)

#### Choose boundaries by responsibility

Apply when adding or restructuring a component or Hook. Extract a coherent UI
contract, reusable composition, or useful update boundary. A Hook extracts React
state/synchronization; a plain transformation needs no Hook. Simple features can
keep logic and markup together. Container/view separation is optional.

**Incorrect (a formatting function gains a misleading React contract):**

```ts
function useRepositoryLabel(name: string, branch: string) {
  return `${name} · ${branch}`;
}
```

**Correct (ordinary calculation stays independently usable):**

```ts
function repositoryLabel(name: string, branch: string) {
  return `${name} · ${branch}`;
}
```

Choose toolkit/product layers and custom component documentation through the
[component guide](../../../src/components/README.md). Component extraction and
Hook extraction are independent decisions; neither file length nor a naming suffix
establishes the right boundary.

Source: [React custom Hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).

### state-ownership

Coordinate state through one explicit owner.

Impact: HIGH — Prevents divergent drafts and duplicated observations.

Source: [rules/state-ownership.md](rules/state-ownership.md)

#### Place state with its coordinating owner

Apply when several controls coordinate selection, drafts, or observations. Keep
interaction state near its consumers and lift it to their closest coordinating
owner. Calling a custom Hook twice creates two independent instances unless it
deliberately connects to a shared source.

**Incorrect (the list and panel cannot share this selection):**

```tsx
function RepositoryList() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | null>(null);
  // Owns a selection unrelated to RepositoryPanel's selection.
}
function RepositoryPanel() {
  const [selected] = useState<string | null>(null);
}
```

**Correct (illustrative child interfaces receive one owner's state):**

```tsx
function RepositoryScreen() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<string | null>(null);
  return <>
    <RepositoryList selected={selected} onSelect={setSelected} />
    <RepositoryPanel selected={selected} />
  </>;
}
```

A dialog can own disclosure and an unsent draft. Shared supervisor/conversation
observations need an explicit owner; see [shared observations](rules/shared-observation-owner.md).

Source: [Sharing state](https://react.dev/learn/sharing-state-between-components).

### derive-during-render

Compute display values instead of synchronizing redundant state.

Impact: MEDIUM — Avoids redundant state and synchronization renders.

Source: [rules/derive-during-render.md](rules/derive-during-render.md)

#### Derive display values during render

Apply when a value is fully determined by current props/state. Calculate it during
render instead of storing a second copy and synchronizing it with an Effect.
Subscribe only to observations that drive output; read event-only values on demand
when that preserves the event's intended target and timing.

**Incorrect (a second state value can lag behind the query):**

```tsx
const [filtered, setFiltered] = useState(items);
useEffect(() => {
  setFiltered(items.filter(item => item.name.includes(query)));
}, [items, query]);
```

**Correct (one source of truth):**

```tsx
const filtered = items.filter(item => item.name.includes(query));
```

An intentionally captured baseline, editable draft, or externally owned observation
is not automatically redundant state. For expensive derivation, consult
[Compiler memoization](rules/compiler-first-memoization.md) and
[responsive rendering](rules/urgent-and-deferred-rendering.md).

Source: [You might not need an Effect](https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect).

### immutable-state-updates

Preserve immutable snapshots and pure queued updates.

Impact: HIGH — Preserves snapshots and queued update semantics.

Source: [rules/immutable-state-updates.md](rules/immutable-state-updates.md)

#### Keep updates immutable and updater functions pure

Apply when changing props/state/observations or computing next state. Treat input
snapshots as immutable. Use a functional updater when the new value depends on
pending state; direct assignments from an event's value remain suitable.

**Incorrect (mutates a retained snapshot):**

```tsx
setRows(previous => {
  previous.push(newRow);
  return previous;
});
```

**Correct (each queued update receives its actual prior state):**

```tsx
setRows(previous => [...previous, newRow]);
// ES2022-compatible copying sort:
const sorted = [...rows].sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
```

Updater functions can be replayed in development: place no IPC, persistence, or
required side effect inside them. Choose newer copying APIs only after checking
TypeScript library declarations and the WebView baseline; compiler optimization
does not make mutation safe.

Sources: [React updaters](https://react.dev/reference/react/useState#updating-state-based-on-the-previous-state),
[array updates](https://react.dev/learn/updating-arrays-in-state),
[TypeScript lib](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/lib.html).

### lazy-initialization

Initialize expensive mounted state without repeated work or commands.

Impact: MEDIUM — Avoids recomputing initialization on each render.

Source: [rules/lazy-initialization.md](rules/lazy-initialization.md)

#### Use pure lazy initialization for expensive initial state

Apply when initial state requires a substantial calculation. Pass an initializer
function rather than evaluating the calculation on every render.

**Incorrect (the calculation runs even after state is initialized):**

```tsx
const [draft] = useState(buildInitialDraft(initialText));
```

**Correct (initializes this mounted state owner):**

```tsx
const [draft] = useState(() => buildInitialDraft(initialText));
```

Initialization is per mount, not once per application lifetime. React can call
initializers extra times in development. Keep them pure and move commands,
subscriptions, and required writes to their proper lifecycle/intent owners.
Changing `initialText` later does not reset this draft: choose an explicit reset
or identity boundary when that is the desired behavior. Cheap literals need no
lazy wrapper. Preference reads additionally follow
[presentation record handling](rules/presentation-records.md).

Source: [React initializers](https://react.dev/reference/react/useState#avoiding-recreating-the-initial-state).

### component-and-list-identity

Preserve component types, domain keys, and deliberate resets.

Impact: HIGH — Prevents state, focus, and resource resets or reassignment.

Source: [rules/component-and-list-identity.md](rules/component-and-list-identity.md)

#### Preserve component and domain identity

Apply to reusable component definitions, reordered lists, or navigation between
domain objects. Keep component types stable, normally at module scope, and use
stable domain keys. Nested component definitions create a new type on each render;
array positions cannot identify records that move.

**Incorrect (reordering can attach a draft to a different conversation):**

```tsx
conversations.map((conversation, index) =>
  <Composer key={index} conversationId={conversation.id} />
);
```

**Correct (identity survives reordering):**

```tsx
conversations.map(conversation =>
  <Composer key={conversation.id} conversationId={conversation.id} />
);
```

React does not pass `key` as a prop: pass action targets explicitly. Ordinary inline
callbacks and JSX expressions are not nested component definitions. Changing a
key can intentionally reset a draft; select that behavior from the feature's
contract rather than prescribing reset or preservation for every screen.

Source: [Preserving/resetting state](https://react.dev/learn/preserving-and-resetting-state).

### refs-and-resources

Distinguish rendered state, mutable handles, and resource lifetimes.

Impact: HIGH — Keeps resource identity independent of disposable memo caches.

Source: [rules/refs-and-resources.md](rules/refs-and-resources.md)

#### Distinguish rendered state from imperative resources

Apply to mutable handles, request generations, timers, and values visible in JSX.
State drives output; refs retain nonrendering mutable information for a mounted
owner. Memo caches can be discarded and do not establish a resource lifetime.

**Incorrect (mutating a ref does not refresh the displayed status):**

```tsx
const pending = useRef(false);
return <button onClick={() => { pending.current = true; }}>
  {pending.current ? "Sending…" : "Send"}
</button>;
```

**Correct (a state update requests the visible change):**

```tsx
const [pending, setPending] = useState(false);
return <button onClick={() => setPending(true)}>
  {pending ? "Sending…" : "Send"}
</button>;
```

The example concerns presentation only, not durable send admission. Set up external
resources in owned Effects with cleanup; ordinary ref reads/writes belong outside
render except supported predictable initialization. A ref bridge can fit an actual
imperative integration, but it must preserve captured action identities.

Source: [React refs](https://react.dev/reference/react/useRef).

## Effects and observations

### events-vs-effects

Separate interaction commands from synchronization.

Impact: HIGH — Prevents view synchronization from replaying user commands.

Source: [rules/events-vs-effects.md](rules/events-vs-effects.md)

#### Send interaction commands through explicit intent paths

Apply when deciding where a command or synchronization belongs. Handle work caused
by a particular interaction in its event/intent path. Effects synchronize external
systems with current inputs; render computes output.

**Incorrect (mounts and dependency changes can replay this command):**

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  void submitDraft(conversationId, draft);
}, [conversationId, draft]);
```

**Correct (illustrative command callback runs on an explicit submit):**

```tsx
function handleSubmit(event: React.FormEvent) {
  event.preventDefault();
  void submitDraft(conversationId, draft);
}
```

The callback still needs [target capture and result handling](rules/async-result-targets.md).
An Effect may read status or install a subscription. Mount, reconnect, and error
recovery retrieve observations; execution/retry decisions belong to the Rust owner
under [the MVP](../../../docs/MVP.md#starting-architecture).

Source: [Separating events from Effects](https://react.dev/learn/separating-events-from-effects).

### synchronization-dependencies

Track actual reactive inputs and independent processes.

Impact: HIGH — Avoids stale synchronization and unrelated resource restarts.

Source: [rules/synchronization-dependencies.md](rules/synchronization-dependencies.md)

#### Match Effect dependencies to each synchronization process

Apply when an Effect reads changing inputs or combines unrelated resource work.
Keep dependencies complete, use actual synchronization inputs, and separate
independent processes with different lifetimes. Change the code before changing
its dependency list.

**Incorrect (the connection remains bound to the initial room):**

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const connection = connect(room.id);
  return () => connection.disconnect();
}, []);
```

**Correct (only the identity actually read controls this resource):**

```tsx
const roomId = room.id;
useEffect(() => {
  const connection = connect(roomId);
  return () => connection.disconnect();
}, [roomId]);
```

Here `connect` is an illustrative stable module function. Other fields read by the
Effect would need their own dependencies. A smaller list is not inherently better.
Splitting independent Effects does not require extracting a custom Hook, and
manually splitting render calculations just to imitate Compiler is unnecessary.

Source: [Removing Effect dependencies](https://react.dev/learn/removing-effect-dependencies).

### effect-events

Read nonreactive Effect values without hiding dependencies.

Impact: HIGH — Preserves resource dependencies without stale event reads.

Source: [rules/effect-events.md](rules/effect-events.md)

#### Use Effect Events only for nonreactive Effect logic

Apply when an event fired from an Effect should see latest committed values without
resynchronizing the external resource. Effect Events have intentionally changing
identity. Call them only from Effects or their callbacks in the owning component;
keep them out of dependencies and arbitrary component/Hook props.

**Incorrect (mute changes reconnect an otherwise unchanged room):**

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const connection = connect(roomId, () => {
    if (!muted) playNotice();
  });
  return () => connection.disconnect();
}, [roomId, muted]);
```

**Correct (for a contract where mute affects notice delivery, not connection):**

```tsx
const onNotice = useEffectEvent(() => {
  if (!muted) playNotice();
});
useEffect(() => {
  const connection = connect(roomId, () => onNotice());
  return () => connection.disconnect();
}, [roomId]);
```

The example's `connect` and `playNotice` are stable illustrative module functions.
`roomId` remains reactive. Latest-value reads must not retarget an admitted action;
use [captured targets](rules/async-result-targets.md) for its completion instead.

Source: [React useEffectEvent](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent).

### subscription-cleanup

Clean up resources even when listener registration resolves late.

Impact: HIGH — Prevents leaked listeners after cleanup or re-setup.

Source: [rules/subscription-cleanup.md](rules/subscription-cleanup.md)

#### Own subscription setup including late registration

Apply to Tauri/browser listeners, timers, and other Effect-owned resources. Cleanup
must cover registration resolving after unmount, not just an already available
handle. Setup/cleanup/re-setup must leave one valid owner.

**Incorrect (cleanup can run before the promise supplies its handle):**

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  let stop: (() => void) | undefined;
  void listen<string>("notice", event => setNotice(event.payload))
    .then(unlisten => { stop = unlisten; });
  return () => stop?.();
}, []);
```

**Correct (late registration tears itself down; rejection is observed):**

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  let disposed = false;
  let stop: (() => void) | undefined;
  void listen<unknown>("notice", event => {
    if (!disposed && typeof event.payload === "string") setNotice(event.payload);
  }).then(unlisten => {
    if (disposed) unlisten();
    else stop = unlisten;
  }).catch(error => { if (!disposed) setError(String(error)); });
  return () => { disposed = true; stop?.(); };
}, []);
```

`listen` is from `@tauri-apps/api/event`; this sketch uses stable React setters.
An event generic supplies types, not payload validation. Reactive subscription
targets still belong in dependencies. Mock registration completion/rejection and
cleanup order in DOM units; real desktop listener behavior needs separate evidence
under [verification policy](../../../docs/agents/verification.md).

Source: [Tauri frontend communication](https://v2.tauri.app/develop/calling-frontend/).

### async-result-targets

Keep late results bound to their original target and generation.

Impact: HIGH — Prevents late responses from overwriting a different view or draft.

Source: [rules/async-result-targets.md](rules/async-result-targets.md)

#### Bind async results to their captured target and generation

Apply to observation reads, sends, native pickers, and other results that can arrive
after navigation or editing. Capture the request's domain identity and relevant
draft/view generation. Separate recording its actual outcome from updating a view
that might no longer own that result.

**Incorrect (selection at completion can identify a different conversation):**

```ts
const result = await send(targetId, text);
recordOutcome(selectedIdRef.current, result);
```

**Correct (illustrative send/outcome interfaces preserve the submitted target):**

```ts
const target = targetId;
const version = draftVersion.current;
const result = await send(target, text);
recordOutcome(target, result);
if (selectedIdRef.current === target && draftVersion.current === version) {
  clearSubmittedDraft();
}
```

Handle rejection and cleanup as well. Suppressing an obsolete view response does
not cancel backend work. Native dialog cancellation returns no selection, and
closing a dialog does not establish that its pending promise was cancelled; guard
late picker results with the dialog/request generation. Durable outcome and retry
ownership remains in Rust, not in this illustrative presentation bookkeeping.

Sources: [React async cleanup](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect#fetching-data-with-effects),
[Tauri dialog API](https://v2.tauri.app/reference/javascript/dialog/).

### shared-observation-owner

Share a source instead of duplicating Hook instances.

Impact: HIGH — Avoids duplicate subscriptions and divergent snapshots.

Source: [rules/shared-observation-owner.md](rules/shared-observation-owner.md)

#### Share one observation owner among consumers

Apply when multiple views need the same supervisor/conversation source. Place its
observation Hook or store at an explicit common owner and distribute its snapshot
and targeted callbacks. A custom Hook's name does not imply shared state.

**Incorrect (two instances install two independent sources):**

```tsx
function Sidebar() { const connection = useConnection(); /* ... */ }
function Diagnostics() { const connection = useConnection(); /* ... */ }
```

**Correct (illustrative child props share one source):**

```tsx
function Shell() {
  const connection = useConnection();
  return <>
    <Sidebar connection={connection} />
    <Diagnostics connection={connection} />
  </>;
}
```

Use context or an [actual external store](rules/external-store-snapshots.md) if consumers
need that distribution model. SWR or another state library is a separate justified
choice, not a required fix for repeated Hook calls. Place a continuing source
outside [visibility-owned subtrees](rules/view-resource-lifetimes.md).

Source: [Custom Hooks share logic, not state](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).

### external-store-snapshots

Integrate actual stores through stable immutable snapshots.

Impact: HIGH — Avoids render loops and missed external updates.

Source: [rules/external-store-snapshots.md](rules/external-store-snapshots.md)

#### Give external stores stable immutable snapshots

Apply when integrating an actual subscribable frontend store with
`useSyncExternalStore`. Keep subscription identity stable where possible and
return the same snapshot reference until the observed data changes.

**Incorrect (every read invents a changed snapshot):**

```ts
const getSnapshot = () => ({ ...currentSnapshot });
```

**Correct (illustrative store publishes a new immutable snapshot on change):**

```ts
type Snapshot = Readonly<{ revision: number; text: string }>;
let currentSnapshot: Snapshot = { revision: 0, text: "" };
const getSnapshot = () => currentSnapshot;
function publish(next: Snapshot) {
  currentSnapshot = next;
  for (const notify of listeners) notify();
}
```

`listeners` represents the store's subscribed callback set; subscription returns
its cleanup. Module ownership in this example is intentional, not a prescription
for global state. Keep snapshots immutable and publish only meaningful changes.
Simple owned observations can remain ordinary React state; introducing a store is
not a prerequisite for calling IPC.

Source: [React useSyncExternalStore](https://react.dev/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore).

### app-initialization

Separate app-load work from mount-owned synchronization.

Impact: MEDIUM — Preserves re-setup without duplicate app-wide initialization.

Source: [rules/app-initialization.md](rules/app-initialization.md)

#### Separate app-load initialization from mount synchronization

Apply to frontend resources intended to exist once per loaded application. An
explicit entry/module initializer can own that lifetime. Mount-owned resources
still need cleanup and re-setup; a flag must not suppress a required second setup.

**Incorrect (after cleanup, remount can leave no observer):**

```tsx
let didSubscribe = false;
useEffect(() => {
  if (didSubscribe) return;
  didSubscribe = true;
  return subscribeToStatus();
}, []);
```

**Correct (the mounted owner can set up again):**

```tsx
useEffect(() => subscribeToStatus(), []);
```

The illustrative module function returns an unsubscribe handle. Truly app-wide
frontend initialization belongs outside this mount Effect when its contract calls
for that lifetime. Neither a module flag nor browser initialization establishes
durable once-only execution across desktop/supervisor restarts; status reads on
mount/reconnect remain valid.

Source: [Application initialization](https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#initializing-the-application).

## Rust/Tauri presentation boundary

### typed-ipc-contracts

Match Rust interfaces and validate untrusted observations.

Impact: HIGH — Prevents malformed or mismatched observations from becoming UI truth.

Source: [rules/typed-ipc-contracts.md](rules/typed-ipc-contracts.md)

#### Validate IPC observations at typed boundaries

Apply to command arguments, replies, and event payloads crossing the Rust/frontend
boundary. Match the Rust contract explicitly. A generic argument or assertion
cannot validate a runtime payload; narrow untrusted data and verify expected kind
and target where the boundary requires it.

**Incorrect (the type parameter silently trusts the reply):**

```ts
type Status = { state: "ready"; owner: string };
const status = await invoke<Status>("example_status");
```

**Correct (illustrative command and minimal schema are explicitly checked):**

```ts
const value = await invoke<unknown>("example_status");
if (typeof value !== "object" || value === null ||
    !("state" in value) || value.state !== "ready" ||
    !("owner" in value) || typeof value.owner !== "string") {
  throw new Error("Invalid status observation");
}
```

`example_status` is an illustrative command, not a new application API. Real
adapters validate the actual schema and domain identities, preserving structured
errors needed by consumers. Toolkit components receive data/callbacks rather than
importing Tauri directly or through application Hooks; see the
[component guide](../../../src/components/README.md).

Sources: [Tauri invoke](https://v2.tauri.app/reference/javascript/api/namespacecore/),
[TypeScript narrowing](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/narrowing.html).

### explicit-targeted-intents

Leave admission, reconciliation, and retries with the Rust owner.

Impact: HIGH — Avoids duplicate work after uncertain replies or reconnect.

Source: [rules/explicit-targeted-intents.md](rules/explicit-targeted-intents.md)

#### Keep execution and reconciliation in the Rust owner

Apply to send, approval, resume, archive, and retry controls. Tauri forwards an
explicitly targeted action and presents its observed status. The owning Rust core
module decides admission, reconciliation, and retries under the
[MVP](../../../docs/MVP.md#starting-architecture).

**Incorrect (an uncertain reply becomes an automatic new submission):**

```ts
try { await submit(action); }
catch { await submit({ ...action, id: crypto.randomUUID() }); }
```

**Correct (illustrative adapter methods retrieve the original action's status):**

```ts
try { await submit(action); }
catch (error) {
  showTransportError(error);
  await readActionStatus(action.id);
}
```

Handle status-read failure visibly too; a second failure grants no retry authority.
The example's methods are placeholders for existing typed owning-module commands,
not new APIs. Retain exact approval identity and the original action payload.
Frontend pending guards improve feedback but do not replace durable duplicate
protection. View mounts and reconnects only retrieve observations.

Source: [Repository execution contract](../../../docs/MVP.md#starting-architecture).

### observation-status

Separate execution evidence, transport, pending feedback, and uncertainty.

Impact: HIGH — Keeps disconnection or UI scheduling from inventing an outcome.

Source: [rules/observation-status.md](rules/observation-status.md)

#### Represent transport and execution evidence separately

Apply to pending/error/loading/status models. Distinguish the authoritative
observation from transport state and local interaction feedback. Preserve retained
observations with an explicit stale/unknown indication when that is the workflow.

**Incorrect (a read failure claims the operation failed):**

```ts
try { await refreshStatus(); }
catch { setExecutionState("failed"); }
```

**Correct (illustrative presentation model keeps the prior observation):**

```ts
type View<T> = {
  observation?: T;
  transport: "connected" | "disconnected";
  error?: string;
};
setView(previous => ({
  ...previous, transport: "disconnected", error: "Status unavailable",
}));
```

Loading, empty, disconnected, stale, failed, and unknown are distinct where the
feature produces them. A Transition's pending flag is rendering feedback, not
provider receipt or completion. Bind action feedback to its actual domain target;
use discriminated unions when they prevent contradictory combinations.

Source: [MVP evidence and recovery](../../../docs/MVP.md#starting-architecture).

## Async coordination

### guard-before-read

Skip unnecessary reads while preserving required effects and errors.

Impact: MEDIUM — Removes unnecessary async waits without changing required work.

Source: [rules/guard-before-read.md](rules/guard-before-read.md)

#### Avoid reads that cheap relevant guards can rule out

Apply when a branch need not observe a remote/IPC value at all. Evaluate cheap
relevant conditions before starting unnecessary reads and await results only in
the branch that uses them.

**Incorrect (loads details even when the panel is closed):**

```ts
const details = await readDetails(id);
if (!isOpen) return;
showDetails(details);
```

**Correct (for a purely optional details read):**

```ts
if (!isOpen) return;
const details = await readDetails(id);
if (isStillCurrent(id)) showDetails(details);
```

The read and view-check callbacks are illustrative. Preserve error handling and
stale-result checks. A guard cannot skip required authorization, reconciliation,
or persistence. Moving an await can change failure selection or side-effect order;
check the actual contract rather than applying this as a mechanical rewrite.

Source: [Vercel guard rule](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/blob/1a2c79d4e6c4a2283dc2c614b6538cbe1ed5ca62/skills/react-best-practices/rules/async-cheap-condition-before-await.md).

### schedule-independent-reads

Schedule actual dependencies with bounded, intentional concurrency.

Impact: MEDIUM — Avoids unnecessary waterfalls while retaining ordering and budgets.

Source: [rules/schedule-independent-reads.md](rules/schedule-independent-reads.md)

#### Schedule reads by their actual dependency graph

Apply when a view needs several observations. Start independent reads together;
start dependent work when its input becomes available. Use native promises and
bound fan-out for growing inputs.

**Incorrect (unrelated observations wait for each other):**

```ts
const snapshot = await invoke<unknown>("supervisor_status");
const pid = await invoke<number>("desktop_pid");
```

**Correct (existing independent command names):**

```ts
const [snapshot, pid] = await Promise.all([
  invoke<unknown>("supervisor_status"),
  invoke<number>("desktop_pid"),
]);
```

Validate replies at the adapter boundary. `Promise.all` rejects on a rejection but
does not cancel sibling work. Choose aggregate versus partial error presentation
from the feature contract; preserve cleanup and target checks. Independent reads
do not establish safe parallel mutations. No dependency helper library is required.

Sources: [Promise.all semantics](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/all),
[Vercel dependency scheduling](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/blob/1a2c79d4e6c4a2283dc2c614b6538cbe1ed5ca62/skills/react-best-practices/rules/async-dependencies.md).

## Rendering and responsiveness

### compiler-first-memoization

Prefer Compiler for routine work and inspect measured exceptions.

Impact: MEDIUM — Keeps optimizations deliberate without relying on cache persistence.

Source: [rules/compiler-first-memoization.md](rules/compiler-first-memoization.md)

#### Let Compiler handle routine memoization

Apply when adding render calculations/callbacks or investigating repeated work.
Check current compiler configuration and diagnostics; coverage is not universal.
Write ordinary pure code first. Add `useMemo`, `useCallback`, or `memo` for measured
benefit or a documented integration need, with complete dependencies.

**Incorrect (routine wrappers obscure a cheap calculation):**

```tsx
const label = useMemo(() => `${name} · ${branch}`, [name, branch]);
```

**Correct (routine new code with Compiler enabled):**

```tsx
const label = `${name} · ${branch}`;
```

Preserve existing deliberate memoization unless the touched change justifies
removing it and checking behavior. A skipped observation Hook may still require
stable callbacks for Effect synchronization. Memo caches are disposable, so use
proper state/ref/resource ownership for correctness. Avoid expensive calculations
in branches that will not display them; extraction is one possible technique.
An omitted default parameter does not change the incoming props compared by that
component's memo boundary, although downstream identity can matter on a render.

Sources: [Compiler defaults](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/07/react-compiler-1#what-should-i-do-about-usememo-usecallback-and-reactmemo),
[Compiler debugging](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler/debugging),
[memo](https://react.dev/reference/react/memo).

### urgent-and-deferred-rendering

Keep inputs urgent while deferring expensive presentation.

Impact: MEDIUM — Keeps interactions responsive without changing action semantics.

Source: [rules/urgent-and-deferred-rendering.md](rules/urgent-and-deferred-rendering.md)

#### Defer expensive presentation while keeping inputs urgent

Apply to slow filtering, history, and change inspection. Keep controlled inputs
and immediate intent feedback urgent. Use a Transition for a nonurgent state
update you own, or a deferred value for an expensive consumer of received input.

**Incorrect (controlled input state is updated as nonurgent):**

```tsx
<input value={query} onChange={event => {
  startTransition(() => setQuery(event.target.value));
}} />
```

**Correct (illustrative results subtree can lag behind typing):**

```tsx
const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query);
return <>
  <input value={query} onChange={event => setQuery(event.target.value)} />
  <HistoryResults query={deferredQuery} stale={query !== deferredQuery} />
</>;
```

Ensure the expensive subtree can skip unchanged urgent renders, using Compiler
first. Explain stale content where it affects actions. Measure calculation versus
render cost: scheduling cannot split one long synchronous calculation. Deferral
does not debounce/deduplicate reads or cancel backend work. Retain authoritative
action status and response ordering. Current React requires another Transition
around post-`await` setters intended to be nonurgent.

Sources: [useDeferredValue](https://react.dev/reference/react/useDeferredValue),
[useTransition](https://react.dev/reference/react/useTransition).

### view-resource-lifetimes

Choose visibility without losing required observations.

Impact: HIGH — Preserves required observations while views are hidden.

Source: [rules/view-resource-lifetimes.md](rules/view-resource-lifetimes.md)

#### Choose visibility by state and resource lifetime

Apply when tabs/panels hide or unmount. Unmounting discards local state and cleans
up Effects; CSS hiding retains mounted resources. Activity preserves state/DOM but
cleans up hidden Effects and re-creates them on reveal.

**Incorrect (a required continuing stream belongs to a hidden Activity):**

```tsx
<Activity mode={visible ? "visible" : "hidden"}>
  <PanelThatOwnsTheSharedStream />
</Activity>
```

**Correct (illustrative props separate observation and presentation ownership):**

```tsx
const stream = useSharedStream();
return <Activity mode={visible ? "visible" : "hidden"}>
  <ConversationPanel stream={stream} />
</Activity>;
```

Draft retention/reset is a feature decision: lift per-target drafts or preserve
appropriate view identity when required. Bound the number of retained views.
Activity is optional, not a universal menu/tab wrapper. Supervisor work and
conversation lifetime are independent of UI visibility.

Source: [React Activity](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity).

### bounded-streams-and-history

Bound retained data, rendered history, and stream processing.

Impact: HIGH — Keeps growing observations from overwhelming the WebView.

Source: [rules/bounded-streams-and-history.md](rules/bounded-streams-and-history.md)

#### Bound stream processing and rendered history

Apply to streamed text/tool events, long history, and large diffs. Bound retained
data and rendered DOM, localize frequent updates, and budget in-flight work. Choose
paging/windowing/virtualization with the feature's accessibility and scroll needs.

**Incorrect (every event retains and renders the entire session forever):**

```tsx
setRows(previous => [...previous, incoming]);
return rows.map(row => <HistoryRow key={row.id} row={row} />);
```

**Correct (illustrative paged presentation exposes a bounded window):**

```tsx
const { page, loadOlder, hasOlder } = useHistoryPage(conversationId);
return <>
  {hasOlder && <button onClick={loadOlder}>Load earlier messages</button>}
  {page.map(row => <HistoryRow key={row.id} row={row} />)}
</>;
```

The example assumes a bounded adapter, not a new storage contract. Authoritative
history and snapshot/cursor recovery remain Rust-owned. Async event callbacks can
finish out of order: preserve sequence/target identity and use the supported
ordered transport when required. Ordered delivery alone does not serialize async
processing; choose explicit processing order or sequence checks. CSS content visibility is optional progressive
enhancement, does not bound DOM/data, and cannot be relied on at Safari 16.4.

Sources: [Tauri channels/events](https://v2.tauri.app/develop/calling-frontend/),
[WebKit content visibility](https://webkit.org/blog/15865/webkit-features-in-safari-18-0/),
[MVP stream bounds](../../../docs/MVP.md#starting-architecture).

### boolean-render-conditions

Prevent numeric guards from leaking text into JSX.

Impact: LOW — Prevents stray zero or NaN output.

Source: [rules/boolean-render-conditions.md](rules/boolean-render-conditions.md)

#### Make numeric JSX conditions explicitly boolean

Apply when the left side of JSX `&&` can be a number or another renderable falsy
value. React renders the expression's result, so a count of zero can become text.

**Incorrect (an empty list renders a stray zero):**

```tsx
{items.length && <ResultList items={items} />}
```

**Correct (the guard produces a boolean):**

```tsx
{items.length > 0 && <ResultList items={items} />}
```

A ternary is also suitable, especially when both branches have meaning. Boolean
`&&` is valid; this rule is about the value produced, not a stylistic ban on it.

Source: [React conditional rendering](https://react.dev/learn/conditional-rendering#logical-and-operator-).

## Loading and bundles

### lazy-surfaces-and-suspense

Load optional surfaces with appropriate local fallbacks.

Impact: MEDIUM — Defers optional code while keeping surrounding UI usable.

Source: [rules/lazy-surfaces-and-suspense.md](rules/lazy-surfaces-and-suspense.md)

#### Load substantial optional surfaces behind local fallbacks

Apply to substantial optional editors/renderers/inspection surfaces. Declare lazy
component types at module scope, with a local loading fallback and an owner for
load failure. Small always-used controls need not be split speculatively.

**Incorrect (a new lazy type is created on every parent render):**

```tsx
function DiffPanel() {
  const Diff = lazy(() => import("./diff-renderer"));
  return <Diff />;
}
```

**Correct (illustrative optional module exports a default React component):**

```tsx
const Diff = lazy(() => import("./diff-renderer"));
function DiffPanel() {
  return <SurfaceBoundary>
    <Suspense fallback={<p>Loading diff…</p>}><Diff /></Suspense>
  </SurfaceBoundary>;
}
```

`SurfaceBoundary` denotes a render error boundary, not an installed library/API.
Keep navigation and usable surrounding content available. Suspense recognizes
supported sources such as lazy code; adding a boundary does not make ordinary
Effect/IPC reads suspend. See [failure handling](rules/render-and-load-failures.md).

Sources: [React lazy](https://react.dev/reference/react/lazy),
[Suspense](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense).

### render-and-load-failures

Distinguish render boundaries, async errors, and cached lazy failures.

Impact: HIGH — Keeps action errors visible and lazy retries deliberate.

Source: [rules/render-and-load-failures.md](rules/render-and-load-failures.md)

#### Handle render failures and async failures at their actual boundaries

Apply to failure isolation for optional surfaces and user actions. Render boundaries
handle descendant render/lazy-load failures. Ordinary event-handler promises and
async callbacks need explicit rejection handling and target-bound feedback.

**Incorrect (a surrounding render boundary cannot handle this ordinary rejection):**

```tsx
<button onClick={() => { void saveDraft(); }}>Save draft</button>
```

**Correct (illustrative async callback handles its own failure):**

```tsx
<button onClick={() => {
  void saveDraft().catch(error => setSaveError(String(error)));
}}>Save draft</button>
```

Capture target/version when the callback can outlive its view, and preserve
uncertain outcomes rather than infer that a failed reply means non-admission.
Use an accessible local error state. React caches a lazy loader's promise and
resolved value; a rejected load is not guaranteed to retry merely by resetting an
error boundary. Design the retry/reload path deliberately; do not recreate lazy
types on every render to simulate recovery. Never replay application actions as
part of render-boundary recovery.

Sources: [React error boundaries](https://react.dev/reference/react/Component#catching-rendering-errors-with-an-error-boundary),
[lazy caching](https://react.dev/reference/react/lazy).

### vite-imports-and-preloading

Keep imports analyzable and preloading free of execution intent.

Impact: MEDIUM — Avoids accidental broad bundles and unsupported loading assumptions.

Source: [rules/vite-imports-and-preloading.md](rules/vite-imports-and-preloading.md)

#### Keep optional imports analyzable and preloading intentional

Apply when choosing optional module/asset loading. Use Vite-supported analyzable
paths or an explicit loader map. Preload code on likely user intent when the
latency benefit warrants it; importing a module must not admit application work.

**Incorrect (the bundler cannot enumerate arbitrary runtime module names):**

```ts
const loadRenderer = (moduleName: string) => import(moduleName);
```

**Correct (illustrative modules are known at build time):**

```ts
const renderers = {
  diff: () => import("./diff-renderer"),
  image: () => import("./image-renderer"),
};
const loadRenderer = (kind: keyof typeof renderers) => renderers[kind]();
```

Vite's normal module entry/import graph manages much loading/preloading work.
Inspect emitted assets before adding classic scripts or resource hints. If a
separate script/resource has an actual consumer, select ordering, load/error
handling, CSP, and browser support for that resource. Drop Next/hydration-specific
recipes; neither a preload nor module initialization is permission to send/start.

Source: [Vite dynamic imports and preload handling](https://vite.dev/guide/features.html#dynamic-import).

### supported-public-imports

Preserve typed package exports while investigating actual bundle costs.

Impact: MEDIUM — Keeps package contracts intact while allowing measured bundle improvements.

Source: [rules/supported-public-imports.md](rules/supported-public-imports.md)

#### Preserve typed public imports until actual cost warrants change

Apply when investigating barrel-import, development-start, or bundle cost. Inspect
package exports/types and actual emitted code before changing paths. Next server
cold-start numbers do not establish a Tauri/Vite bundle problem.

**Incorrect (an assumed internal icon path can break exports or types):**

```ts
import Folder from "lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/folder";
```

**Correct (supported named icon import):**

```ts
import { Folder } from "lucide-react";
```

Lucide documents tree-shakable named imports and Vite prebundles dependencies.
These facts are not a guarantee that every package's barrels are free. If actual
analysis identifies a costly entry, choose a supported narrower export or other
measured remedy. Do not add untyped declarations merely to silence a deep-import
problem. Icon composition/styling remains governed by
[shadcn](../shadcn/SKILL.md) and the component guide.

Sources: [Lucide React](https://lucide.dev/guide/react/),
[Vite dependency prebundling](https://vite.dev/guide/dep-pre-bundling).

## Browser integrations

### layout-measurement

Group layout reads and invalidating writes in imperative integrations.

Impact: MEDIUM — Avoids repeated forced layout in imperative integrations.

Source: [rules/layout-measurement.md](rules/layout-measurement.md)

#### Separate layout reads from invalidating writes

Apply when an editor, scroller, or other imperative integration must measure DOM.
Prefer declarative CSS/classes for ordinary visual state. When measurements are
necessary, group reads and writes so each write does not force another read layout.

**Incorrect (each height change can invalidate the next width read):**

```ts
for (const element of elements) {
  element.style.height = `${container.offsetWidth}px`;
}
```

**Correct (one measurement serves the batch):**

```ts
const width = container.offsetWidth;
for (const element of elements) element.style.height = `${width}px`;
```

The example intentionally uses imperative owned elements; it is not a reason to
mutate arbitrary React-managed DOM. Choose an Effect/observer with cleanup when
integrating external layout, and account for resize and hidden/unmounted nodes.
Use layout Effects only when pre-paint measurement is actually required; they
block painting. Actual WebView layout/focus behavior needs desktop evidence.

Sources: [Layout thrashing](https://web.dev/articles/avoid-large-complex-layouts-and-layout-thrashing),
[useLayoutEffect](https://react.dev/reference/react/useLayoutEffect).

### passive-event-listeners

Match listener cancellation behavior to the interaction.

Impact: LOW — Lets scrolling proceed without waiting for cancellable handlers.

Source: [rules/passive-event-listeners.md](rules/passive-event-listeners.md)

#### Use passive listeners when the interaction only observes

Apply when introducing wheel/touch listeners. If the handler never needs to cancel
the default interaction, mark it passive and retain owned cleanup.

**Incorrect (an observation-only wheel listener remains potentially blocking):**

```ts
element.addEventListener("wheel", observeWheel, { passive: false });
```

**Correct (for a handler that only observes):**

```ts
element.addEventListener("wheel", observeWheel, { passive: true });
// On owner cleanup:
element.removeEventListener("wheel", observeWheel);
```

A gesture/zoom implementation that requires `preventDefault` needs an active
listener instead; passive handlers cannot cancel it. Keep handler and capture
identity consistent during removal. This rule does not introduce global listeners
or override a toolkit's accessible interaction contract.

Source: [DOM passive listener option](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-addeventlisteneroptions-passive).

### owned-attachment-resources

Release preview resources without confusing them with durable content.

Impact: MEDIUM — Avoids leaking URLs or confusing previews with durable content.

Source: [rules/owned-attachment-resources.md](rules/owned-attachment-resources.md)

#### Own attachment preview resources through cleanup

Apply to image/file preview URLs and subscriptions. Create external resources in
an owned lifecycle and release them when replaced/unmounted, after consumers no
longer need them. A preview URL is not durable attachment storage.

**Incorrect (every render allocates a URL that is never revoked):**

```tsx
return <img src={URL.createObjectURL(file)} alt="Attachment preview" />;
```

**Correct (resource ownership sketch; use only if blob previews are allowed):**

```ts
function openPreview(file: File): () => void {
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(file);
  try {
    const closePreview = mountPreview(url);
    return () => {
      try { closePreview(); }
      finally { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); }
    };
  } catch (error) {
    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
    throw error;
  }
}
```

`mountPreview` is an illustrative preview adapter that returns its teardown; the
caller owns the returned cleanup, including replacement/unmount and setup failure.
Gate stale preview results, expose load failure, and retain accessible names.
Check Tauri CSP and asset permissions before choosing blob/data/native asset URLs;
the current image policy does not automatically allow blob URLs. Choose a
compatible preview path rather than broadly relaxing policy. Durable transcript
and attachment writes remain with Rust storage under the
[MVP](../../../docs/MVP.md#starting-architecture).

Sources: [File API object URL lifetime](https://www.w3.org/TR/FileAPI/#lifeTime),
[Tauri CSP](https://v2.tauri.app/security/csp/).

### safe-rendered-content

Keep provider text and URLs within explicit rendering contracts.

Impact: HIGH — Prevents transcript text from acquiring DOM or application authority.

Source: [rules/safe-rendered-content.md](rules/safe-rendered-content.md)

#### Keep provider content as data at the rendering boundary

Apply to transcript/tool output, paths, diffs, Markdown, and attachment metadata.
Render ordinary content as text. If a feature requires HTML/Markdown, select a
renderer with an explicit raw-HTML and URL policy; no renderer is chosen merely
by adding this rule.

**Incorrect (provider text is treated as trusted HTML):**

```tsx
<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: providerText }} />
```

**Correct (plain transcript content remains text):**

```tsx
<pre className="whitespace-pre-wrap">{providerText}</pre>
```

For richer content, review supported link schemes, image sources and native-open
callbacks against Tauri capabilities/CSP. Displayed links, file paths, or suggested
tool operations cannot authorize native commands or approval. Preserve exact
application-owned targets in explicit intent paths. This rule adds no sanitizer,
Markdown library, native permission, or remote-resource requirement.

Sources: [React raw HTML caveats](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/common#dangerously-setting-the-inner-html),
[Tauri capabilities](https://v2.tauri.app/security/capabilities/).

### timers-and-long-tasks

Budget optional work with supported scheduling and cleanup.

Impact: MEDIUM — Keeps optional work responsive without delaying required effects.

Source: [rules/timers-and-long-tasks.md](rules/timers-and-long-tasks.md)

#### Budget optional long tasks and own scheduled callbacks

Apply when measured noncritical work blocks input. Bound/chunk work or consider an
appropriate worker. If idle scheduling fits, check WebView support, provide a
fallback and cancellation, and retain target/generation checks. A timeout only
defers a long task; it does not make that task interruptible.

**Incorrect (an unsupported idle API becomes the only execution path):**

```ts
window.requestIdleCallback(() => buildOptionalPreview());
```

**Correct (illustrative cancellable fallback for small optional work):**

```ts
function scheduleOptional(work: () => void): () => void {
  if (typeof window.requestIdleCallback === "function") {
    const id = window.requestIdleCallback(work, { timeout: 1000 });
    return () => window.cancelIdleCallback(id);
  }
  const id = window.setTimeout(work, 0);
  return () => window.clearTimeout(id);
}
```

The owner calls the returned cancellation function on cleanup and guards already
started work. Do not rely on idle opportunity for required identity persistence,
execution, reconciliation, or cleanup. Use controlled time in applicable DOM units;
that evidence does not measure actual WebView responsiveness.

Source: [Idle callback support and semantics](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/requestIdleCallback).

### svg-and-animation-tradeoffs

Preserve visual/accessibility contracts when optimizing assets.

Impact: LOW — Avoids unsupported GPU claims and damaged asset geometry.

Source: [rules/svg-and-animation-tradeoffs.md](rules/svg-and-animation-tradeoffs.md)

#### Treat SVG and animation changes as measured visual tradeoffs

Apply when SVG complexity or animation is an actual rendering cost. Inspect the
asset and WebView behavior before choosing wrapper transforms, reduced path
precision, or a different asset. Keep accessible naming, layout, focus and reduced
motion behavior under the component contract.

**Incorrect (loading animation ignores the reduced-motion contract):**

```tsx
<span className="inline-flex animate-spin"><LoaderIcon /></span>
```

**Correct (illustrative nonessential animation respects reduced motion):**

```tsx
<span className="inline-flex motion-safe:animate-spin"><LoaderIcon /></span>
```

The icon is an illustrative existing accessible loading indicator. A wrapper can
change layout/semantics and does not establish GPU acceleration. Coordinate
rounding must preserve appearance at intended scales; benchmark/compare the actual
asset. Prefer supported Lucide imports and existing toolkit animation facilities;
their sizing and styling contracts remain in
[the component guide](../../../src/components/README.md).

Sources: [Tailwind reduced motion](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/hover-focus-and-other-states#prefers-reduced-motion),
[Vercel SVG precision tradeoff](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/blob/1a2c79d4e6c4a2283dc2c614b6538cbe1ed5ca62/skills/react-best-practices/rules/rendering-svg-precision.md).

## Installed UI integrations

### base-ui-props-and-refs

Forward the complete composed behavior and DOM ref.

Impact: HIGH — Keeps focus, event handling, and accessible trigger behavior intact.

Source: [rules/base-ui-props-and-refs.md](rules/base-ui-props-and-refs.md)

#### Preserve Base UI composition props and refs

Apply when a custom React component receives Base UI `render` composition props.
Forward received props and ref to the intended single DOM element. The selected
foundation uses `render`; Radix `asChild` examples require translation.

**Incorrect (drops the library's handlers, attributes, and ref):**

```tsx
function Trigger({ children }: React.ComponentPropsWithRef<"button">) {
  return <button>{children}</button>;
}
```

**Correct (React 19 forwards the ref through these props):**

```tsx
function Trigger(props: React.ComponentPropsWithRef<"button">) {
  return <button {...props} />;
}
```

When adding handlers or styles, use supported composition/merging behavior rather
than overwriting incoming behavior. Base UI `render` merges refs, whereas its
`mergeProps` utility alone retains the rightmost ref. Preserve the intended
interactive element and check keyboard/focus behavior. Layer/style choices remain
owned by [the component guide](../../../src/components/README.md) and
[shadcn](../shadcn/SKILL.md); this rule adds no wrapper requirement.

Source: [Base UI composition](https://base-ui.com/react/handbook/composition).

### controlled-inputs-and-submission

Keep typing synchronous and form intents distinct.

Impact: HIGH — Preserves typing, validation, and native form semantics.

Source: [rules/controlled-inputs-and-submission.md](rules/controlled-inputs-and-submission.md)

#### Keep controlled input updates synchronous and submission explicit

Apply to composer/configuration fields and form controls. A controlled text input
keeps a defined string value and synchronously reflects user edits. Keep form
submission in an explicit intent path, and mark non-submit buttons accordingly.

**Incorrect (an unrelated picker button submits the containing form):**

```tsx
<form onSubmit={submit}>
  <button onClick={browse}>Choose folder</button>
</form>
```

**Correct (the two interactions have distinct semantics):**

```tsx
<form onSubmit={submit}>
  <button type="button" onClick={browse}>Choose folder</button>
  <button type="submit">Register</button>
</form>
```

Do not switch between controlled and uncontrolled values; use `value={text ?? ""}`
when absence should mean an empty controlled draft. Keep the input update urgent
and defer expensive consumers instead. Preserve labels, help/error associations,
focus, and pending feedback through existing Field/Input contracts. Native dialog
results only update the intended draft; they do not implicitly submit it. DOM
units use semantic queries and controlled dependency outcomes under
[verification policy](../../../docs/agents/verification.md).

Sources: [React input](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/input),
[Base UI forms](https://base-ui.com/react/handbook/forms).

### tailwind-static-classes

Make complete variant class candidates discoverable.

Impact: MEDIUM — Prevents runtime variants whose CSS is absent from the bundle.

Source: [rules/tailwind-static-classes.md](rules/tailwind-static-classes.md)

#### Keep Tailwind class candidates discoverable

Apply to conditional classes and component variants. Tailwind detects complete
class strings in source; it does not evaluate JavaScript interpolation. Map finite
choices to complete semantic classes or existing `cva` variants.

**Incorrect (the full class name never appears in source):**

```tsx
const className = `text-${muted ? "muted-foreground" : "foreground"}`;
```

**Correct (each possible utility is statically present):**

```tsx
const className = muted ? "text-muted-foreground" : "text-foreground";
```

For actual composition use existing `cn`/`cva` APIs and preserve their types. Truly
dynamic values may need a supported CSS variable/style strategy; check CSP and
the property's ownership. Source registration and theme changes belong in the
current Tailwind 4 configuration, not a parallel legacy config. The
[component guide](../../../src/components/README.md) owns token/variant and
styling decisions; this rule concerns CSS generation, not new visual conventions.

Source: [Tailwind source detection](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files).

### base-ui-csp-integration

Integrate injected elements with the actual desktop CSP.

Impact: HIGH — Avoids broken controls or blanket policy relaxation.

Source: [rules/base-ui-csp-integration.md](rules/base-ui-csp-integration.md)

#### Integrate Base UI injected elements with the desktop CSP

Apply when adding controls that inject style/script elements, such as relevant
Scroll Area or aligned Select configurations. Inspect the current Tauri CSP and
installed Base UI docs before selecting integration behavior.

**Incorrect (broadly allowing inline code to silence a component issue):**

```text
script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'
```

**Correct (one documented option when equivalent external CSS is supplied):**

```tsx
import { CSPProvider } from "@base-ui/react/csp-provider";
<CSPProvider disableStyleElements>{controls}</CSPProvider>;
```

Disabling injected style elements requires supplying their needed behavior in an
allowed stylesheet, then checking the actual controls. A matching nonce strategy
is another option only with a properly integrated CSP; inventing a fixed nonce is
not sufficient. `CSPProvider` governs injected elements, not ordinary client-side
JavaScript style assignments. The current app is client-rendered, so SSR style
attribute caveats must not be copied as a blanket prohibition. This rule authorizes
no automatic CSP, capability, or component changes.

Sources: [Base UI CSP Provider](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/csp-provider),
[Tauri CSP](https://v2.tauri.app/security/csp/).

## Storage and algorithms

### presentation-records

Validate evolving preferences while preserving uncertain-action identity.

Impact: HIGH — Keeps schema migration from erasing uncertain work.

Source: [rules/presentation-records.md](rules/presentation-records.md)

#### Validate and evolve presentation records without losing action identity

Apply when reading/writing desktop preferences or changing their shape. Keep
records small, validate decoded data, and choose migration/version behavior for
the actual compatibility need. Distinguish discardable preferences from retained
identities needed to retrieve authoritative action status.

**Incorrect (every decode/migration failure deletes recovery identity):**

```ts
try { return migrate(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) ?? "null")); }
catch { localStorage.removeItem(key); return null; }
```

**Correct (illustrative decoder preserves unsupported or corrupt records):**

```ts
type Decoded<T> = { kind: "ok"; value: T } | { kind: "unreadable" };
function readRecord<T>(key: string, decode: (raw: unknown) => T): Decoded<T> {
  try {
    return { kind: "ok", value: decode(JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(key) ?? "null")) };
  } catch { return { kind: "unreadable" }; }
}
```

The caller selects visible recovery for unreadable records; successful decoding is
not authoritative execution evidence. Preserve original action IDs/payloads across
migration and handle read/write failure according to the workflow. A cache miss
cannot prove non-admission. Presentation storage does not replace Rust-owned
durable transcripts/metadata. Avoid repeated synchronous reads during render;
initialize or subscribe through an explicit owner.

Sources: [localStorage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage),
[MVP durability](../../../docs/MVP.md#starting-architecture).

### owned-bounded-caches

Define cache identity, invalidation, capacity, and ownership.

Impact: MEDIUM — Avoids stale results and unbounded lifetime outside React.

Source: [rules/owned-bounded-caches.md](rules/owned-bounded-caches.md)

#### Give shared caches an owner, invalidation, and bounds

Apply when measurement justifies caching beyond routine Compiler memoization.
Define the key's complete identity/revision, invalidation, capacity/lifetime, and
other writers. Component-owned initialized state is often enough for preferences.

**Incorrect (a file name alone aliases different revisions forever):**

```ts
const cache = new Map<string, string>();
function remember(path: string, rendered: string) { cache.set(path, rendered); }
```

**Correct (illustrative one-entry cache is bounded and revision-specific):**

```ts
type Entry = { workspace: string; path: string; revision: string; rendered: string };
let last: Entry | undefined;
function cached(workspace: string, path: string, revision: string) {
  return last?.workspace === workspace && last.path === path && last.revision === revision
    ? last.rendered : undefined;
}
function remember(entry: Entry) { last = entry; }
```

The actual cache belongs to a chosen resource owner and clears on relevant context
changes. A one-entry cache is an example, not a required capacity. Suppressing
duplicate reads cannot replace Rust action deduplication or snapshot/cursor
reconciliation. Account for storage events or other writers if that source exists.

Sources: [React memoization scope](https://react.dev/learn/react-compiler/introduction),
[storage event semantics](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/storage_event).

### indexes-and-extrema

Choose algorithms for actual growing-data workloads.

Impact: MEDIUM — Avoids unnecessary repeated scans or sorts on growing data.

Source: [rules/indexes-and-extrema.md](rules/indexes-and-extrema.md)

#### Choose data structures for repeated lookup and selection work

Apply to measured repeated joins/membership or growing history/change data. An
index can avoid scanning the same collection for each item. Account for rebuild
cost, key uniqueness, ownership, and readability before replacing short arrays.

**Incorrect (large repeated membership scans):**

```ts
const visible = rows.filter(row => selectedIds.includes(row.id));
```

**Correct (when the workload warrants building the index):**

```ts
const selected = new Set(selectedIds);
const visible = rows.filter(row => selected.has(row.id));
```

Measure index construction as well as lookups. Maps need a duplicate-key policy;
silently keeping the last value may change a join that previously selected the
first. An extremum can be found in one pass rather than sorting the entire input;
preserve tie, empty-input and comparison semantics. Compiler can optimize repeated
render work, but it does not establish the right domain algorithm or index bounds.

Sources: [Set](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Set),
[Vercel extrema example](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/blob/1a2c79d4e6c4a2283dc2c614b6538cbe1ed5ca62/skills/react-best-practices/rules/js-min-max-loop.md).

### behavior-preserving-hot-loops

Optimize measured loops without changing values, effects, or errors.

Impact: LOW — Keeps micro-optimizations from changing selected values or errors.

Source: [rules/behavior-preserving-hot-loops.md](rules/behavior-preserving-hot-loops.md)

#### Preserve behavior when optimizing measured hot loops

Apply when profiling identifies repeated iteration/property access as meaningful
cost. Consider cheap decisive checks, early exits, combined passes, or local reuse
only with equivalent values, ordering, validation, and observable effects.

**Incorrect (the rewrite changes empty-string filtering):**

```ts
// Original:
const names = users.filter(user => user.active).map(user => user.name).filter(Boolean);
// Claimed equivalent, but retains active users' empty names:
const rewritten = users.flatMap(user => user.active ? [user.name] : []);
```

**Correct (if a combined pass is justified and name is a string):**

```ts
const names: string[] = [];
for (const user of users) {
  if (user.active && user.name) names.push(user.name);
}
```

Fewer source-level passes do not prove faster execution. Preserve first-versus-last
error selection, getters/proxy behavior, and comparator semantics. Cache property
access or combine passes only where it matters; clear separate transforms remain
valid. Use application requirements, not a performance recipe, to choose behavior.

Sources: [Array flatMap](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/flatMap),
[Vercel original example](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/blob/1a2c79d4e6c4a2283dc2c614b6538cbe1ed5ca62/skills/react-best-practices/rules/js-flatmap-filter.md).

### regexp-reuse-and-state

Reuse expressions without leaking mutable matching state.

Impact: LOW — Avoids allocation costs without introducing stateful matching bugs.

Source: [rules/regexp-reuse-and-state.md](rules/regexp-reuse-and-state.md)

#### Reuse regular expressions only with explicit state semantics

Apply when repeated expression construction is a measured cost. A constant pattern
can live outside a hot loop, but global/sticky expressions carry mutable `lastIndex`.
Choose that state deliberately rather than blindly hoisting every expression.

**Incorrect (repeated tests can alternate because the shared regex is global):**

```ts
const hasDigit = /\d/g;
const matches = values.map(value => hasDigit.test(value));
```

**Correct (a stateless membership test needs no global flag):**

```ts
const hasDigit = /\d/;
const matches = values.map(value => hasDigit.test(value));
```

When global/sticky iteration is required, reset or isolate matching state according
to its owner. Dynamic patterns need correct escaping and bounded/admissible input;
turning arbitrary user text into a regex changes literal-search semantics. A
shared cache of dynamic expressions additionally follows
[cache ownership and bounds](rules/owned-bounded-caches.md).

Source: [RegExp test and lastIndex](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/RegExp/test#description).

## Completion

For changed stateful/effectful boundaries, account for owner, target identity, and
applicable stale, cleanup, and failure paths. Review components through their guide
for layer, tokens/variants, documentation, and accessible interaction contracts.
Resolve findings or explain concrete tradeoffs. Apply improvements within the
requested scope; a rule is not an instruction to rewrite unrelated working code.

Select checks through repository policy. Static checks and controlled DOM units
establish different evidence from actual WebView responsiveness, accessibility,
and native-provider qualification. Report performed checks, unperformed
qualification, and justified convention exceptions separately.
